status_summary: The United States continues to decline to support the proposal by WTO members to launch Appellate Body appointments: at the Dispute Settlement Body meeting of 2026-09-25 it said its fundamental concerns with dispute settlement had not been addressed and that the proposal (WT/DSB/W/609/Rev.26) would restore the conditions that produced them; a trade-press account of the 2026-06-23 meeting reports the proposal was then backed by 130 members and blocked for the 98th time. USTR's WTO reform paper of 2026-03-23 (WT/GC/W/998) does not address the Appellate Body, proposes that essential security measures be self-judging and not adjudicated, and suggests interim and, if needed, non-WTO plurilateral agreements among subsets of members, not an alliance limited to liberal democracies. No successor organization or Global Free Trade Alliance proposal was found.

title: Restore WTO dispute settlement or build a successor alliance of liberal democracies
uncertainties: WTO.org pages could not be fetched, so the 130-member and 98th-time figures rest on a Third World Network account; the US statement of 2026-09-25 was read on USTR's site. Two searches for a Global Free Trade Alliance proposal found none, but absence rests on limited searching. The essay itself notes that both prior administrations kept the blockade, so this is a continuation rather than a reversal; it is staged diverged because the operative US position at each meeting is opposite to restoring the Appellate Body. The reform paper's non-WTO plurilaterals are not restricted to liberal democracies and are not a successor body, so they do not meet the fallback recommendation.
